title: Simple quotient ⇔ maximal normal subgroup (the IsMaxNorm/IsSimpleGroup bridge)
description: Open question oq-01 of the Jordan-Hölder branch asks to contribute JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G) to Mathlib, whose 'main challenge' is generalizing the combinatorial IsMaxNorm predicate to IsSimpleGroup (K ⧸ H) directly. The parent entry only ASSERTS (in a comment) that IsMaxNorm H K is equivalent to IsSimpleGroup (K ⧸ H.subgroupOf K) 'by the correspondence theorem'. This formalization PROVES that bridge, axiom-free, in the essential case K = ⊤: a normal subgroup N ◁ G has a simple quotient G ⧸ N if and only if N is a maximal normal subgroup of G. The proof routes through Mathlib's fourth isomorphism / correspondence theorem (QuotientGroup.comapMk'OrderIso) rather than re-deriving the lattice correspondence, giving a short, clean equivalence that settles the crux the open question identifies.

meta.author: Jordan, Hölder; Lean formalization original (researcher-10)
meta.assumptions: None. Every result is machine-checked with 0 axioms and 0 sorries (foundational propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only). Built on Mathlib's QuotientGroup.comapMk'OrderIso (correspondence theorem), comap_map_mk', normal_comap, ker_mk'. NOTE: this proves the K = ⊤ case (N ◁ G); the fully general K/subgroupOf version — working inside the subtype group ↥K, the 'quotient typeclass issues' the open question flags — and the actual Mathlib upstreaming remain open.

IsMaximalNormal.isSimpleGroup_quotient / .of_isSimpleGroup_quotient: the two directions as reusable lemmas

conclusion.summary: The combinatorial maximality predicate IsMaxNorm and the categorical simplicity predicate IsSimpleGroup of the quotient are equivalent, for K = ⊤: G ⧸ N is simple iff N is a maximal normal subgroup. The forward direction pushes a normal M ⊇ N into the quotient (it must be ⊥ or ⊤, giving M = N or M = ⊤); the reverse pulls a normal subgroup of G ⧸ N back through mk' and uses injectivity of the correspondence map. This is the bridge the parent entry asserted but did not prove.
implications: Confirms IsMaxNorm and IsSimpleGroup carry the same information for K = ⊤, supporting the upstreaming goal.
The correspondence theorem (comapMk'OrderIso) makes the equivalence a short, robust proof.
openQuestions: Generalize to arbitrary K via H.subgroupOf K, navigating the subtype-group quotient typeclasses — the part the open question flags as the main obstacle.
Actually contribute JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G) and this bridge upstream to Mathlib.
